**Speciallæger** (specialist doctors) are a key professional group within the Danish psychiatric healthcare system, playing a central role in the diagnostic assessment of ADHD. Within the framework of the national ADHD database and quality reporting, their participation in diagnostic conferences is considered a critical standard for clinical quality.

The [[styregruppen|Styregruppen]] (steering committee) has unanimously agreed that specialist doctors should be present for the majority of diagnostic conferences [^src1]. This requirement is formalized in [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]], a national quality metric which tracks the number of patient pathways where a diagnostic ADHD conference involving a specialist doctor in child and adolescent psychiatry is held within 120 days of the assessment's start [^src3]. Due to its importance, Indicator 3 has been designated as a primary focus area for the steering committee in the coming year [^src2].

However, the exclusive diagnostic authority of specialist doctors is currently under debate. The Danish healthcare system is facing systemic challenges, including rising patient volumes and a documented shortage of specialist doctors [^src2]. In response, legislative changes have been introduced that permit [[specialpsykolog|specialpsykologer]] (specialist psychologists) to independently make diagnoses [^src2]. This shift has sparked institutional discussions regarding the distribution of interdisciplinary competencies, the standardization of assessment pathways, and how best to integrate the competencies of specialist psychologists to improve clinical quality and patient outcomes. The ongoing evaluation of the specialist doctors' role reflects a broader tension between traditional clinical practices, evolving legislative frameworks, and national quality goals in Danish child and adolescent psychiatry.
